handDesc.handNote: Main text and any darker interventions are distinguished where observed. No individual historical correcting hands are inferred from tonal contrast in monochrome photographs.

origin.p: The supplied BnF IIIF manifest dates the manuscript to 1001–1100. The catalogue dating is not a date assigned to individual interventions.

surrogates.p: The original full-resolution digital images and enlarged crops were inspected for this first pass. Gallica source reuse conditions apply. No text was populated from LL or another witness.

projectDesc.p: Source-grounded first reading of all 48 annotated verse positions, with manuscript-specific spellings and observed interventions. A different agent subsequently inspected all source verses and every evidence note; see revision record and second-pass ledger.

correction.p: No silent emendation from an edition or another witness. Local uncertain letters use unclear, irrecoverable text or signs use gap. Observed above-line letters use add. Tonal distinctions use hi without an invented underlying erased text or historical hand. Manuscript annotations use note type manuscript, distinct from editorial evidence notes.

normalization.p: One source-oriented display. Ordinary allographs, long s, and capitals are represented in legible Latin types. Word boundaries are editorially segmented; no indentation whitespace is inserted inside verse mixed content. Selected ligatures and abbreviation signs are declared typographic approximations; explicit expansions remain in TEI rather than a separate reading mode. This is not a facsimile-perfect inventory of every minute stroke.

punctuation.p: Significant observed punctuation is retained schematically, without adding systematic modern sentence punctuation.

segmentation.p: Each l represents a verse and physical written line at its canonical poem position. Elegiac couplets and even-line indentation are editorial display grouping. Page breaks follow the photographed left/right physical pages. Facsimile zones reproduce the existing annotation rectangles unchanged; they may include neighbouring ink and exclude marginal annotations.

interpretation.p: First-pass evidence notes are a working queue for an independent agent, not assignments for the human editor. Genuine source uncertainty remains local; consequential unresolved interpretation is distinguished from ordinary observation.

revisionDesc.change: Independent second-agent source review of all 48 verses and every editorial note. Qualified the first iliades at40, retaining other conservative first-pass readings after direct inspection. Extensively faded lines, especially36, remain provisional; no erased text or alternative-witness wording is supplied. No human approval is implied.
Completed first reading from source images and enlarged crops, with line coverage and evidence notes. Independent second reading not yet performed.

div.head: Independently reviewed source notes
div.note: The four-line marginal heading is represented AD VIRUM / SERUAN / TĒ UX / OREM. VIRUM is faint; the marked TĒ is expanded as TEM in SERUANTEM. The large D begins the poem. Physical heading line breaks are retained with word continuity rather than silently adding spaces.
The middle of ingenio is faded; local unclear preserves the tentative reading. No replaced underlying text is inferred.
Selected et ligatures occur inside metu and later verbal forms, as well as the conjunction. Explicit schematic glyphs and expansions preserve their distinction from a silently expanded text.
The phrase bene corpus is markedly faint. It remains a tentative local reading; tonal contrast is not evidence of a recoverable erasure.
The short phrase following custodiri reads ne uelit; it is retained without silently altering the wording.
The opening Obsequio uinces is faded at the foot of image87. The first line on the next left page,13, also has a faint extended phrase equum contra sua uincla tenacem. Both retain uncertainty.
The first words Constitit ut are faint; the following concessas sensit habenas is more securely legible.
The visible spelling is iuuenis. The word is not regularized to another inflection from grammatical expectation.
The word seruatur is faint. At26 the opening Cura uocat is similarly faded. The readings remain local uncertainties.
The opening Nescioquid is tentative. At29 the central fit quam uir seruat is faint and retained locally in unclear.
The end of32 is read siqua potest but is faded. No invisible letters or unrelated witness text are asserted as certain.

The central phrase externae corpora gentis is markedly faint. Lines35–36 also have extended faded text: ego dicere feci and In laudem serui casta sit illa tui. These readings remain tentative after independent source inspection.

The end of37 and much of39 are faint: quem laedit adultera coniunx and non sunt sine crimine nati. The first iliades after Romulus at40 is now locally unclear after independent inspection; the later iliadesque remus remains more legible.

A dark sign resembling a curved B occurs in the left margin beside the final couplet. Its function and exact glyph identity are not established; metamark with an illegible sign records its presence without assigning a textual reading or hand. The first iliades in the verse remains locally unclear after independent inspection of its faint later strokes.

The opening Quo tibi is faded near the gutter on the right page; Non possunt at42 is also faint. The physical page break is before41, despite the small x-coordinate overlap of some existing rectangles with the opening gutter.
Verse48 is followed by the next poem beginning Nox erat. The complete48-position coverage and poem boundary are observed in the source, not inferred solely from annotations.
